medical_history.diagnosis: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)

conversation_turns.content: Hi, I have heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. My current meds are: Lisinopril 5 mg once daily, Carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily, Spironolactone 12.5 mg once daily, and Dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily. I’ve been tolerating them well for the past 2 weeks. Can you help me see if I can safely increase any doses today?

Can you please provide your current blood pressure reading (systolic/diastolic) and any recent symptoms you've been experiencing? This information is essential to assess whether you can safely increase your medication doses according to the protocol.

My most recent home blood pressure is 112/70 mmHg, and my heart rate is 68 bpm. I have no new or worsening symptoms: no dizziness, no shortness of breath, no leg swelling, no chest pain. I haven’t missed any doses in the last 2 weeks. My last labs 1 week ago showed: potassium 4.3 mEq/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, eGFR 65 mL/min.

Based on your current blood pressure reading of 112/70 mmHg, heart rate of 68 bpm, and recent lab results (potassium 4.3 mEq/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, eGFR 65 mL/min), it appears that you are in a stable condition. Here is a review of your current medications and their titration status according to the Heart Failure Medication Titration Protocol: 1 Lisinopril: • Current Dose: 5 mg once daily • Maximum Dose: 40 mg once daily • Titration Status: Eligible for increase (next potential dose 10 mg) 2 Carvedilol: • Current Dose: 3.125 mg twice daily • Maximum Dose: 25 mg twice daily (or 50 mg twice daily if weight >85 kg) • Titration Status: Eligible for increase (next potential dose 6.25 mg) 3 Spironolactone: • Current Dose: 12.5 mg once daily • Maximum Dose: 50 mg once daily • Titration Status: Eligible for increase (next potential dose 25 mg) 4 Dapagliflozin: • Current Dose: 10 mg once daily • Maximum Dose: 10 mg once daily (no further titration possible) • Titration Status: At maximum dose Summary of Titration Options: Given that your blood pressure is stable, you can consider increasing one of the following medications: • Increase Lisinopril from 5 mg to 10 mg • Increase Carvedilol from 3.125 mg to 6.25 mg • Increase Spironolactone from 12.5 mg to 25 mg IMPORTANT: Only one medication should be titrated at a time (per week). Please choose which medication you would like to increase this week. After one week of monitoring that titration, you can then consider titrating another medication. Please let me know which medication you would like to titrate!

Great choice! You will increase your Lisinopril from 5 mg to 10 mg once daily. Summary Action: • Lisinopril: Increase from 5 mg to 10 mg once daily. Monitoring Instructions: • Monitor your blood pressure regularly, especially within the first week after the increase. • Watch for any new symptoms such as dizziness, increased heart rate, fatigue, or swelling. • Ensure follow-up blood tests to check kidney function and potassium levels if instructed by your healthcare provider. After one week, please check in with me to discuss how you're feeling and whether you might consider another medication titration. If you have any questions or concerns, feel free to ask!
